text:
jordan: :rotating_light: Observed a spike of 502/504s from hosted streaming endpoints (eu-west) starting ~10m ago. Customers reporting aborted streams and `keepalive reset` in logs. Opening triage.
ivy-support: reported by 3 customers, support ticket numbers linked. One customer sent a curl repro showing connection closed after ~30s. They see lots of partial responses.
maya-sre: looking at LB metrics — upstream connections are getting RST from the auth-proxy pool. Connection reuse dropped, open conns to model-backend rose from 200 -> 1400 in 5m.
ben-eng: can you paste the auth-proxy logs? guessing token refresh or 504s from sidecar.
jordan: snippet from gateway logs:
```
[2026-03-17T12:08:21Z] stream_id=abc123 ERROR keepalive: write failed: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-17T12:08:22Z] upstream=auth-proxy status=502 backend=rt-infer-03 conn=1345
[2026-03-17T12:08:23Z] client=10.2.4.5 stream_close reason=client_disconnect
```
lee: seeing tok-refresh spikes coinciding with these times. auth-proxy process shows GC and threads hitting socket limits.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-3249876543. Pager notified. :white_check_mark:
ivy-support: Customer impact estimate: 8% of streaming requests in eu-west failed, mainly long-running streams >25s.
maya-sre: quick mitigation plan: 1) add temporary rate-limit on long-lived streams to protect proxy, 2) increase upstream keepalive timeout and conn limits on auth-proxy, 3) enable fallback to shorter chunking window for streaming clients.
ben-eng: prepared a canary patch to auth-proxy to reuse connections more aggressively and avoid token refresh per request. Can push to eu-west canary.
lee: also seeing a cascade where large KV-cache misses cause backend CPU spike, leading to delayed responses and client timeouts. Reducing default batch_size might help short-term.
jordan: steps taken: increased auth-proxy max_sockets from 1500 -> 4000; bumped keepalive from 15s -> 60s; deployed config to eu-west edge in two clusters.
ops-bot: Deploy started by ben-eng to eu-west-canary. Build: bld-2026-324 (auth-proxy conn-reuse).
ben-eng: canary is up. Early metrics: error rate on canary nodes down ~60% vs baseline.
maya-sre: rolling to 50% of eu-west. Monitoring p50/p95/p99 latency and open connections.
ivy-support: updated affected customers with mitigation status and ETA for permanent fix. :thumbsup:
jordan: request for evidence for postmortem: logs for RST, auth-proxy GC traces, token refresh timings, batcher queue lengths. Assign owners?
maya-sre: I'll own the SRE investigation (auth-proxy + LB). lee will own backend batcher investigation. ben-eng will own auth-proxy code changes and perf testing. ivy-support will collate customer impact and comms.
lee: immediate action item — reduce default streaming batch_size from 128 -> 32 for next 24h in eu-west to reduce CPU pressure. I'll coordinate with ben for deploy window.
ben-eng: noted. Also will add a temporary circuit that rejects streams older than 120s with 429 to avoid pileup.
ivy-support: customers asked for timeline. Proposed: full rollout and monitoring through next 2 hours, then schedule hotfix release with tests tomorrow morning.
jordan: ACTIONS:
- maya-sre: collect auth-proxy GC and socket metrics + timeline (by EOD)  
- lee: run repro harness with reduced batch_size and share perf numbers (by 3h)  
- ben-eng: submit PR for conn-reuse + circuit + tests, link to deploy playbook (by EOD)  
- ivy-support: update customer comms & compile affected request IDs (ongoing)
- All: postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC (please RSVP)

maya-sre: initial hypothesis: token refresh path + aggressive stream retention caused socket exhaustion and RSTs -> 5xx cascade. Need root cause for increased token refresh frequency.
lee: could be a regression in token caching header introduced in last auth-proxy release (r321). I'll diff config.
ben-eng: I'll revert the part of r321 that changed token header expiry handling if tests fail.
jordan: temporary workaround status: error rate down ~55% after keepalive + canary patch, customer-reported errors decreasing. Still monitoring p99.
ivy-support: saved affected customer examples in ticket. Will push interim workaround docs for customers that can chunk their streams client-side.
ops-bot: Reminder: incident channel will be archived after postmortem. Use #incidents for followups.
ben-eng: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/auth-proxy/pull/432 — includes conn reuse, socket pool tuning, and a regression test harness.
maya-sre: collecting logs now. Found correlation: auth-proxy downtime windows coincide with large batcher GC cycles on rt-infer nodes. Setting up heap/proc sampling.
lee: repro script (local) attached:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  "https://eu-west.api.redwood/v1/stream?model=rt-small" &
done
```
Run with batch_size=128 to repro. With batch_size=32, repro rate <5%.
jordan: OK. We'll keep this channel for live updates. Postmortem owners listed in issue INC-3249876543-POST. Thanks all. :heart:
ben-eng: final note — add e2e streaming load tests to CI to prevent this regression.
ivy-support: acknowledged. I'll include that in the postmortem doc.
maya-sre: closing live triage for now; monitoring will continue. If error rate creeps up >3x baseline, re-open immediate paging.
jordan: documented timeline and tentative RCA in INC-3249876543-POST. Meeting invite sent. :calendar:
